report_name: AdaptHealth Data Breach Exposes Personal and Health Info of 4.1M

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attacker used legitimate, stolen credentials from a third-party contractor to access AdaptHealth's cloud-based patient management applications.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The attacker accessed and exfiltrated a large volume of patient data, including protected health information (PHI), from cloud-based platforms used for patient management and document storage.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor likely exfiltrated the stolen patient data over standard web protocols from the compromised cloud environment.

identities.name: AdaptHealth
identities.description: A U.S. provider of medical equipment that suffered a data breach affecting 4,115,802 individuals after an attacker accessed its cloud-based patient management systems via a compromised third-party contractor account.

identities.name: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
identities.description: The U.S. government agency to which AdaptHealth reported the data breach, as required under HIPAA.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud Authentication Pattern
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Successful Sign-In With Failed Conditional Access
id: 2b8c1f3a-9e7d-4b0f-8c1d-6a5b4c3d2e1f
status: experimental
description: Detects a successful user sign-in to a cloud service that also had a conditional access policy failure. This could indicate a successful MFA bypass or a misconfigured policy being exploited.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/4-1-million-impacted-by-adapthealth-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-10
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: 0
    ConditionalAccessStatus: 'failure'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a successful cloud account login that simultaneously failed a conditional access policy check, which could indicate a compromised account or MFA bypass, consistent with the access method used in the AdaptHealth breach.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud Data Sharing Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Creation of Public Sharing Link for Sensitive Data
id: 9d8c7b6a-5f4e-4d3c-2b1a-0987654321fe
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a public or anonymous sharing link for documents or folders within a sensitive location, such as one containing PHI.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/4-1-million-impacted-by-adapthealth-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-10
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.t1567
level: high
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.sharepoint
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'SecureLinkCreated'
    ObjectId|contains:
      - '/PHI/'
      - '/PatientData/'
      - '/PII/'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a public sharing link for data in a cloud environment, a potential method for data exfiltration as seen in the breach where large volumes of patient data were stolen.
